_readme: Photographs of the temples and mathas this community names, gathered from Wikimedia Commons under free licences. Regenerate with `npm run media:temples`. Every entry carries its photographer, its licence and the page it came from; the site renders all three wherever the image appears, which is a condition of using them. Do not hand-edit the image blocks — the script owns them.

items.name: Shri Mangueshi Temple
items.blurb: Shiva as Mangirish. The deity was carried from Kushasthali — Cortalim, on the Zuari — to Priol in the sixteenth century, and the seven-storey deepstambha in front of it is the one most Saraswats picture when they picture a Goan temple.

items.name: Shri Shantadurga Temple
items.blurb: Parvati in the act of making peace between Shiva and Vishnu. Originally of Keloshi (Quelossim); more Saraswat households name Shantadurga as their kuladevata than any other deity.

items.name: Shri Mahalasa Temple
items.blurb: Vishnu in the Mohini form, brought from Verna to Mardol. The brass lamp tower in the courtyard is lit on Kojagiri Purnima and is among the tallest in Goa.

items.name: Shri Ramnathi Temple
items.blurb: Shiva as Ramnath, moved inland from Loutolim. The silver screen before the sanctum is worked with scenes that families come specifically to see.

items.name: Shri Nagesh Maharudra Temple
items.blurb: Shiva as Nagnath. An inscription on the temple tank dates the site to 1413, which makes it one of the few Goan temples standing on ground it never had to leave.

items.name: Shri Saptakoteshwar Temple
items.blurb: The tutelary deity of the Kadamba kings of Goa, formerly of Divar island. Rebuilt at Narve in 1668 under Shivaji, and the only Goan temple of its period with a distinctly Maratha profile.

items.name: Shri Damodar Temple
items.blurb: Shiva as Damodar, originally of Mathagram — Margao. The Kushavati river beside it is held to cure, and the Gulal festival here is attended by Hindu and Christian families alike.

items.name: Shri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
items.blurb: Vishnu as Narasimha, with Lakshmi. The tank and the sloping laterite steps below the temple are seventeenth-century.

items.name: Shri Kamakshi Temple
items.blurb: Parvati as Kamakshi, brought from Raia in Salcete. The Rayeshwar and Laxmi Narayan shrines share the compound.

items.name: Shri Chandreshwar Bhutnath Temple
items.blurb: Shiva on the Chandranath hill above Paroda, where the sanctum is built so that moonlight falls on the linga. The climb is part of the visit.

items.name: Shri Vijayadurga Temple
items.blurb: Durga as the victorious. A smaller temple than most in this list, and the kuladevata of a correspondingly close-knit set of families.

items.name: Shri Navadurga Temple
items.blurb: Durga in her nine forms. The temple at Madkai is known for the tradition of putting questions to the deity through the palanquin.

items.name: Shri Mallikarjun Temple
items.blurb: Shiva as Mallikarjun, deep in Canacona where the Portuguese conquest arrived late and the temple was never moved.

items.name: Shri Shantadurga Kunkalikarin Temple
items.blurb: The Shantadurga of the Cuncolim families, moved to Fatorpa after the revolt of 1583. The Shisharanni festival still returns the deity towards Cuncolim once a year.

items.name: Shri Vithal Temple
items.blurb: Vishnu as Vitthala, standing on the brick — the Pandharpur form, carried into Goa by families who kept the Varkari connection.

items.name: Shri Ananta Temple
items.blurb: Vishnu reclining on Shesha, at Savoi Verem. One of the few reclining Vishnu images in Goa.

items.name: Shri Bhagavati Temple
items.blurb: Durga as Bhagavati, in Pernem north of the Chapora — the New Conquests, annexed late enough that the temples there were left standing.

items.name: Shri Venkataramana Temple
items.blurb: The principal temple of the GSB families who settled along the coastal Karnataka strip. Not a Goan temple at all — which is the point of it: it is where the families who left built again.

items.name: Shri Chitrapur Math
items.blurb: The spiritual home of the Chitrapur Saraswats — the Bhanaps — at Shirali in Uttara Kannada. The guru parampara begins with Shrimat Parijnanashram Swami I, around 1708.

items.name: Shri Saunsthan Gaudapadacharya, Kavale
items.blurb: Traditionally the oldest of the Saraswat mathas, tracing to Shri Gaudapadacharya. Smarta, and the seat named by GSB, Rajapur and Kudaldeshkar households alike.

items.name: Shri Kashi Math Samsthan
items.blurb: The Vaishnava seat established in 1542 under Shrimad Yadavendra Tirtha, with its principal branch at Walkeshwar in Mumbai — which is where most of the diaspora families of this lineage actually go.

items.name: Shri Gokarn Partagali Jeevottam Math
items.blurb: Founded around 1475 by Shrimad Narayana Teertha at Partagali in Canacona. A principal Vaishnava seat of the Goud Saraswat community.
